_note: Batch 1 draft (author pass, pre-review). 5 sci-fi theme tag sets. Requirements: sci-fi, artifacts, alien civilizations (need NOT be fallen). Resource tie-ins welcome but not mandatory for all. Psychic OPTIONAL (per Sam) — varied here. Breadth is the goal: each should produce worlds that don't feel like siblings of the others or of the original fallen-civ/psychic theme (#0).

sets.title: The Ones Still Watching
sets.hook: The aliens aren't dead — they're alive, ancient, and deciding right now whether humanity is worth keeping; the artifacts are gifts whose true meaning you must decode before you misread one into a war.
sets.artifact_flavor: Diplomatic gifts and lent technology whose function is a test; misusing one is an insult, decoding one is an overture.
sets.distinct_from_siblings: Aliens are PRESENT and reactive, not a tomb to excavate. The drama is reading intent across an unbridgeable gap, not piecing together a fall.

sets.title: The Green Cathedral
sets.hook: The 'civilization' is one vast living organism that covers a world; its artifacts are grown, not built, and to use them is to be slowly colonized by something that thinks you are now part of it.
sets.artifact_flavor: Bio-relics — seeds, spores, grown tools, symbiotes — that grant power while rewriting the user; the resource IS the organism's living tissue.
sets.distinct_from_siblings: Organic, intimate, transformation-horror. Resource exploitation is literally harvesting a living mind's body — but the horror is becoming, not extinction.

sets.title: The Patient Engine
sets.hook: A self-replicating machine civilization went quiet ten thousand years ago; its artifacts are cores and code-relics that still run, and the central question is whether the silence is death — or patience.
sets.artifact_flavor: Functional but corrupted machine cores; each runs a fragment of a vast intent; activating one is a gamble on what it wakes.
sets.distinct_from_siblings: Cold, logical, recursive dread. No biology, no psychic — the threat is intelligence without empathy, and the mystery is intent, not cause-of-death.

sets.title: Objects Out of Order
sets.hook: An alien civilization fought a war through time itself; their artifacts are objects out of their own sequence — effects that precede causes — and assembling the timeline means deciding which version of history actually happened.
sets.artifact_flavor: Anachronisms — an object older than its maker, a relic that remembers a future; each rewrites what you thought the prior artifacts meant.
sets.distinct_from_siblings: The mystery is non-linear: clues arrive out of order and contradict, and 'why they fell' may not have happened yet. Resource element deliberately minimal.

sets.title: We Were the Aliens
sets.hook: The 'alien' ruins fit human hands too well; the artifacts are memory-cores, and piecing them together reveals the colonists are the descendants of the very civilization they're excavating — and why their ancestors chose to forget.
sets.artifact_flavor: Memory-cores and sealed records; each reveal is a recovered memory that re-frames the colony's own identity and the reason for the great forgetting.
sets.distinct_from_siblings: The 'alien' civilization turns out to be us. The mystery is introspective — who are we and what did we choose to bury — rather than xeno-archaeology of a stranger.
